questions.enonce_markdown:
Of what relevance was the Martyrdom of Stephen to the Christian faith?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Stephen was one of the Seven chosen to serve at tables in the Jerusalem church (Acts 6:1-6), a Greek-speaking Jewish believer "full of faith and of the Holy Spirit" who also worked wonders and spoke with wisdom. Accused of speaking against the Temple and the Law, he was stoned to death (Acts 6-7). His death was the first Christian martyrdom recorded in Acts and carries lasting significance.

**1. A model of faithful witness.** The Greek word *martys* means witness, and the later use of "martyr" comes from such cases. Stephen did not deny Christ even when his life was at stake and so became a model of courage for the church.

**2. A model of Christ-like death.** Stephen's last words resemble those of Jesus on the cross: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" and "Lord, do not hold this sin against them" (Acts 7:59-60; compare Luke 23:34, 46). He sees the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:55-56). His death shows the believer's forgiveness of enemies and the hope of heaven.

**3. The teaching of his speech.** Stephen's long address (Acts 7) reviews the history of Israel, from Abraham to Solomon, and argues that God is not confined to a house made by hands, as in the Temple (Acts 7:48-50), and that the people have repeatedly resisted the Holy Spirit and killed the prophets, and have now killed the Righteous One. His speech helped the church to understand that its faith was not bound to the Temple and the old forms of worship.

**4. The spread of the church.** After his death a great persecution arose in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria (Acts 8:1). Those who were scattered preached the word wherever they went (Acts 8:4). Philip took the Gospel to Samaria (Acts 8:5-25), and others reached Antioch where Gentiles were also addressed (Acts 11:19-21). In this way persecution led to the fulfilment of the commission to be witnesses in Judea, Samaria and to the end of the earth (Acts 1:8).

**5. The link with Paul.** The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul, who approved of the killing (Acts 7:58; 8:1). Saul became the leading persecutor and then, after his conversion, the apostle to the Gentiles (Acts 9). Many Christians have seen Stephen's prayer and example as part of the background of Paul's later change.

**6. A warning of the cost of faith.** The story reminds Christians that following Christ may bring suffering, which agrees with the teaching of Jesus (Luke 9:23; John 15:20). Through the centuries Christians have honoured Stephen as the first martyr and have drawn strength from his example when facing persecution.

**Conclusion.** The martyrdom of Stephen was relevant in several ways: it gave an example of faithful witness and forgiveness, it clarified the relation of the faith to the Temple, it scattered the believers and so widened the mission, and it prepared the way for Paul. Its importance for the Christian faith is therefore very great.
